Building software from source

To compile ScopeFun from source on Windows, follow these steps.

Prerequisites:

- Python: https://www.python.org/downloads/
- CodeBlocks IDE: https://www.codeblocks.org/downloads/binaries/
- MSYS2: https://www.msys2.org/

Windows setup:

1. Install MSYS2 in the default folder, C:\msys64.
2. After installation, run the MSYS2 64-bit shell and update packages:

	pacman -Syu

3. Add C:\msys64\mingw64\bin to the Windows PATH.
4. Open the MSYS2 MinGW 64-bit shell and install the required packages:

	pacman -Su
	pacman -S git
	pacman -S make
	pacman -S msys/automake-wrapper
	pacman -S msys/autoconf
	pacman -S mingw-w64-x86_64-gcc
	pacman -S mingw-w64-x86_64-make
	pacman -S mingw-w64-x86_64-nsis
	pacman -S mingw-w64-x86_64-cmake
	pacman -S mingw-w64-x86_64-gdb

Build steps:

1. Clone the repository and create a build directory:

	git clone https://gitlab.com/scopefun/scopefun-software.git
	mkdir scopefun-software/build
	cd scopefun-software/build

2. Build the libraries in MSYS2 MinGW 64-bit:

	cd ~/scopefun-software/build
	cd ../lib/libusb-1.0.25 && aclocal && automake && cd .. && cd ../build
	cmake -G "MinGW Makefiles" -D SCOPEFUN_BUILD_TYPE="Release" -D CPACK_SOURCE_ZIP="false" ..
	mingw32-make package

	SCOPEFUN_BUILD_TYPE can be either Release or Debug.

3. Build the CodeBlocks project after the libraries are complete:

	cd scopefun-software
	mkdir codeblocks-build
	cd codeblocks-build
	cmake -G "CodeBlocks - MinGW Makefiles" -D SCOPEFUN_BUILD_TYPE=Release ..

4. Open the generated ScopeFun.cbp project in CodeBlocks, build it, then select the ScopeFun target and run it.

The installation package is generated in the build folder, and the Python API module (.pyd) is generated in build/source.
